The purpose of the Transition Services Agreement is to facilitate an orderly transition of the Business from Seller to Buyer and to enable Buyer to establish independent operational capability with respect to the functions and services described in Exhibit H.

The Transition Period shall commence on the Closing Date and shall not exceed eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date (the \"**Maximum TSA Term**\"). Each individual Transition Service shall be provided for the period specified in Exhibit H with respect to such Transition Service, which period shall in no event exceed the Maximum TSA Term.

For the avoidance of doubt, the Transition Period shall expire no later than the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date, unless the parties mutually agree in writing to extend the Transition Period for any individual Transition Service, provided that no such extension shall exceed an additional six (6) months beyond the Maximum TSA Term for any individual Transition Service. Any such extension shall be documented in a written amendment to the Transition Services Agreement executed by both parties. No automatic renewal or extension mechanism shall be included in the Transition Services Agreement.

The Transition Services shall be provided in a manner and at a level of quality substantially consistent with the manner and level of quality at which such services were provided to the Business during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the Closing Date. Seller shall allocate sufficient resources and qualified personnel to provide the Transition Services in accordance with the foregoing standard throughout the Transition Period.
**Section 7.12(b) --- Service Fees**

All fees payable by Buyer to Seller under the Transition Services Agreement for the Transition Services (the \"**TSA Fees**\") shall be calculated on a cost-plus basis, reflecting the Service Provider\'s Fully-Loaded Cost (as defined in Section 1.1) of providing each Transition Service, plus a markup not to exceed ten percent (10%) of such Fully-Loaded Cost.

The estimated Fully-Loaded Cost and estimated monthly TSA Fees for each category of Transition Services are set forth in Exhibit H. Such estimates are based on Seller\'s actual cost experience for the twelve (12) months ended December 31, 2024, and shall be subject to adjustment in the Transition Services Agreement to reflect actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred during the Transition Period, provided that any such adjustment shall be calculated in accordance with the Fully-Loaded Cost definition and shall not exceed the estimated amounts set forth in Exhibit H by more than five percent (5%) without Buyer\'s prior written consent.

In no event shall the markup applied to any category of Transition Service exceed ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost for such category. This limitation shall apply to each category of Transition Service individually and not solely on an aggregate or blended basis across all categories.

Any fees for services that are not described in Exhibit H but that are requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in writing (\"**Additional Services**\") shall be priced on terms to be mutually agreed by the parties, which pricing may include a markup in excess of ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with a good faith estimate of the Fully-Loaded Cost and proposed markup for any Additional Service prior to the commencement of such Additional Service.
**Section 7.12(c) --- Termination of Individual Services**

Buyer or Seller may terminate any individual Transition Service upon not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other party, specifying the Transition Service to be terminated and the effective date of such termination. Such notice shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.1 of this Agreement.

Upon termination of any individual Transition Service, Buyer\'s obligation to pay TSA Fees with respect to such terminated Transition Service shall cease as of the effective date of termination, subject to Buyer\'s obligation to pay all TSA Fees accrued through such effective date and to reimburse Seller for any non-cancelable costs or commitments that Seller incurred prior to receipt of the termination notice in reasonable reliance on the continuation of such Transition Service, provided that Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such non-cancelable costs.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the Transition Services Agreement provides for a notice period different from the ninety (90) day period specified in this Section 7.12(c), the notice period set forth in this Agreement shall control. The parties acknowledge and agree that this Section 7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum notice period applicable to the termination of individual Transition Services, and any provision in the Transition Services Agreement purporting to require a longer or shorter notice period shall be of no force or effect.
**Section 7.12(d) --- Limitation of Liability**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that the aggregate liability of the Service Provider (and its Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents) to the Service Recipient under or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient to the Service Provider during the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient (the \"**TSA Liability Cap**\").

For purposes of calculating the TSA Liability Cap during the first twelve (12) months of the Transition Period, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated based on the total TSA Fees actually paid by the Service Recipient from the Closing Date through the date on which the applicable claim is first asserted in writing by the Service Recipient. Thereafter, the TSA Liability Cap shall be calculated on a rolling twelve (12) month basis, measured from the date of assertion of the applicable claim and looking back twelve (12) months from such date.
The limitation set forth in this Section 7.12(d) shall not apply to:
> \(i\) claims arising from a party\'s fraud or willful misconduct;
> \(ii\) a party\'s breach of its confidentiality obligations under the Transition Services Agreement; or

> \(iii\) a party\'s indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims arising out of the provision or receipt of Transition Services, to the extent such third-party claims result from the indemnifying party\'s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.

In no event shall either party be liable to the other party for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or in connection with the Transition Services Agreement, regardless of whether such damages are based on contract, tort, strict liability, or any other theory, and regardless of whether such party has been advised of the possibility of such damages; provided, however, that this sentence shall not limit the liability of a party with respect to third-party claims for which indemnification is provided under the Transition Services Agreement.

The parties acknowledge and agree that the foregoing limitations on liability reflect the parties\' agreement regarding the allocation of risk under the Transition Services Agreement, and that neither party would have entered into this Agreement without such limitations.
**Section 7.12(e) --- Cooperation**

During the Transition Period, Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own capability to perform the Transition Services independently and to reduce its reliance on Seller for the provision of such Transition Services as promptly as reasonably practicable. Buyer shall dedicate appropriate internal resources, including qualified personnel and financial resources, to the transition effort and shall develop and implement a transition plan in consultation with Seller.

Seller shall cooperate in good faith with Buyer\'s efforts to transition the Transition Services to Buyer\'s own systems, personnel, and third-party providers. Such cooperation shall include reasonable knowledge transfer, documentation of processes and procedures, and making Seller\'s personnel reasonably available for consultations during normal business hours.
Nothing in this Section 7.12 or the Transition Services Agreement shall require Seller to:
> \(i\) maintain any employee in employment or any contractor engagement solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services;

> \(ii\) acquire, license, or maintain any hardware, software, or other technology solely for the purpose of providing Transition Services, except to the extent that Seller was licensing or maintaining such technology for the benefit of the Business as of the Closing Date and the cost of such license or maintenance is included in the Fully-Loaded Cost;
> \(iii\) provide any Transition Service in a manner that would require Seller to violate any applicable Law or breach any contractual obligation to a third party; or
> \(iv\) disclose any trade secrets, proprietary information, or confidential business information of Seller that does not relate to the Business.
**Section 7.12(f) --- Service Standard; No Prioritization**

The Transition Services Agreement shall provide that Seller shall provide the Transition Services in a manner substantially consistent with the manner and quality at which such services (or substantially similar services) were provided to or on behalf of the Business during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the Closing Date. The parties acknowledge that Seller\'s historical practices, methodologies, systems, and resource levels as applied to the Business during such twelve (12) month period shall serve as the benchmark for the required level of service under the Transition Services Agreement.

Nothing in the Transition Services Agreement shall obligate Seller to provide Transition Services at a level of quality, timeliness, or responsiveness that exceeds the level provided to the Business during such twelve (12) month period, or to prioritize the provision of Transition Services over services that Seller provides for its own account, for its retained business divisions, or for its other business units. Seller shall not be required to adopt new methodologies, systems, standards, or best practices in connection with the provision of Transition Services that were not in use with respect to the Business during such twelve (12) month period.

The parties acknowledge and agree that Seller is not a professional services provider and that the Transition Services are being provided on an accommodation basis to facilitate the orderly transition of the Business to Buyer. Accordingly, the parties agree that the standard of care applicable to the provision of Transition Services shall be measured solely by reference to Seller\'s historical performance with respect to the Business and shall not be measured against any external industry standard, best-practice benchmark, or professional services standard.
**Section 7.12(g) --- Cross-Border Services**

To the extent that any Transition Services are provided in connection with the operations of the Monterrey Facility or involve the processing of personal data of employees located in Mexico, the Transition Services Agreement shall include commercially reasonable provisions to ensure compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including:

> \(i\) the IMMEX Program requirements applicable to the Monterrey Facility, including provisions addressing the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the allocation of responsibility for IMMEX reporting obligations during the Transition Period, and compliance with applicable customs and trade requirements; and

> \(ii\) Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) and its Regulations, including provisions addressing the lawful basis for the transfer and processing of personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, the implementation of appropriate privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*), and the establishment of adequate data protection safeguards.

Seller and Buyer shall cooperate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of responsibilities under the IMMEX Program during the Transition Period, including with respect to the maintenance of the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification, the timely filing of all required IMMEX reports, and the management of temporary importation records. The parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the transition of IMMEX Program obligations from Seller to Buyer is completed in a manner that avoids any lapse in the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX certification or any violation of applicable Mexican customs Law.

No claim for indemnification based upon a breach of any representation or warranty may be asserted after the expiration of the applicable survival period, except that any claim for which a Claim Notice (as defined in Section 10.3) has been delivered to the Indemnifying Party prior to the expiration of such survival period shall survive until the final resolution thereof.

The covenants and agreements of the parties contained in this Agreement that by their terms are to be performed after the Closing (including, without limitation, the obligations set forth in Section 7.8 (Employee Matters), Section 7.12 (Transition Services Agreement), Section 7.15 (Tax Matters), and Section 7.17 (Further Assurances)) shall survive the Closing in accordance with their respective terms, and any claim for indemnification based upon a breach of any such post-Closing covenant may be asserted at any time prior to the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations.

**Description of Services:** Continued access to and support of Seller\'s SAP S/4HANA enterprise resource planning system for all Business-related modules (including finance and controlling, procurement and materials management, production planning and manufacturing execution, sales and distribution, and human capital management modules); network infrastructure support for the Facilities, including LAN/WAN administration, firewall management, and connectivity monitoring; cybersecurity monitoring and incident response services, including threat detection, vulnerability scanning, and security event management; email and collaboration tools administration, including Microsoft 365 platform management and user account administration; help desk support (Tier 1 and Tier 2) for Business-related IT issues; data backup and disaster recovery services, including regular backup execution, backup verification, and recovery testing; and management of Business-related IT assets, including hardware inventory tracking and end-of-life replacement coordination.

**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately thirty-one (31) full-time equivalent personnel, including ERP administrators, network engineers, cybersecurity analysts, database administrators, and help desk staff.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$340,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$374,000
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note:** Buyer acknowledges that Seller\'s SAP S/4HANA system is an integrated enterprise platform that serves all of Seller\'s business divisions, including the Architectural Coatings Division, the Performance Polymers Division, and Seller\'s corporate functions. Seller shall provide Buyer with access to Business-related modules and data only, and Buyer shall not access, view, or attempt to access or view any data, modules, or system components that are not related to the Business. Seller shall have no obligation to modify, customize, or develop new functionality within the SAP S/4HANA system for the benefit of Buyer, and Seller retains sole discretion over the administration, configuration, and upgrade schedule of the SAP S/4HANA system, provided that Seller shall provide Buyer with reasonable advance notice of any planned system changes that would materially affect the Transition Services. Buyer\'s access to the SAP S/4HANA system shall terminate upon the earlier of (i) the expiration or termination of this Category of Transition Services or (ii) Buyer\'s successful migration to its own enterprise resource planning system.
**[Category 3 --- Human Resources]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Payroll processing and administration for Transferred Employees during the Transition Period, including payroll calculation, payroll tax withholding and reporting (federal, state, and local), direct deposit administration, and W-2 preparation; benefits administration (medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term and long-term disability, and 401(k) plan) during any transition period before Buyer establishes its own benefit plans and enrolls Transferred Employees therein; HRIS system access and support, including maintenance of employee records, employee self-service portal administration, and standard HR reporting; workers\' compensation claims management and reporting; and general HR advisory support, including guidance on employment law compliance, employee relations matters, and leave of absence administration, in each case to the extent consistent with the services historically provided by Seller\'s corporate human resources function to the Business.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately eighteen (18) full-time equivalent personnel, including payroll specialists, benefits administrators, HRIS analysts, and HR generalists.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$125,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$137,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note Regarding Monterrey Facility:** With respect to Transferred Employees located at the Monterrey Facility, Seller shall process payroll and administer benefits in accordance with applicable Mexican Law, including the Federal Labor Law (*Ley Federal del Trabajo*) and applicable social security (*Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social*, or \"IMSS\") and housing fund (*Instituto del Fondo Nacional de la Vivienda para los Trabajadores*, or \"INFONAVIT\") requirements. The parties shall include appropriate provisions in the Transition Services Agreement to address compliance with Mexico\'s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (*Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares*) and its Regulations in connection with the processing of personal data of Monterrey Facility employees, including the preparation and distribution of appropriate privacy notices (*avisos de privacidad*) and the establishment of data transfer mechanisms compliant with such Law.
**[Category 4 --- Supply Chain & Procurement]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Raw material sourcing and procurement under Seller\'s existing master supply agreements (to the extent such agreements are assignable or otherwise available for Buyer\'s benefit during the Transition Period, and subject to any required third-party consents); logistics coordination for inbound and outbound shipments, including carrier management, freight rate negotiation, and shipment tracking; warehouse management services at the shared warehouse facility located within the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility, including receiving, put-away, picking, packing, and shipping operations for Business-related inventory; inventory management support, including cycle counting, inventory valuation, and stock replenishment planning; and vendor relationship management during the transition to Buyer\'s own supply chain organization, including facilitating introductions between Buyer and key suppliers and assisting with the transition of purchasing relationships.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately fourteen (14) full-time equivalent personnel, including procurement specialists, logistics coordinators, warehouse supervisors, and inventory analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$210,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$231,000
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note:** Buyer acknowledges that certain of Seller\'s master supply agreements contain change-of-control, assignment, or consent provisions that may require third-party consents in connection with the provision of procurement services to Buyer. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain any required consents; provided, however, that Seller shall not be required to pay any consideration to any third party, agree to any material modification of any master supply agreement, or incur any material obligation or liability in order to obtain such consents. In the event that any required consent cannot be obtained, the parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify alternative arrangements that provide Buyer with substantially equivalent access to the relevant raw materials or supplies.
**[Category 5 --- Regulatory & EHS Compliance]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Environmental permit maintenance and compliance support for the Greenville and Monterrey Facilities, including permit renewal tracking, compliance calendar management, and regulatory agency correspondence; Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) compliance monitoring and reporting, including workplace inspection support, incident investigation, and recordkeeping; Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) reporting obligations related to the Business, including Toxic Release Inventory (TRI) reporting, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) compliance, and Clean Air Act permit reporting; workplace safety program administration, including safety training program coordination, personal protective equipment program management, and safety committee facilitation; environmental audit support, including coordination of internal and third-party environmental audits; and hazardous materials management compliance, including hazardous waste manifesting, storage area inspections, and transportation of dangerous goods compliance.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately eight (8) full-time equivalent personnel, including environmental compliance specialists, safety engineers, and regulatory affairs analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$95,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$104,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.

**Special Note Regarding Monterrey Facility:** With respect to the Monterrey Facility, Regulatory & EHS Compliance services shall include support for compliance with applicable Mexican environmental standards (*Normas Oficiales Mexicanas*, or \"NOM\" standards), including NOM-001-SEMARNAT-2021 (wastewater discharge) and NOM-043-SEMARNAT-1993 (particulate emissions), and assistance with maintaining the Monterrey Facility\'s IMMEX Program certification. The parties shall include appropriate provisions in the Transition Services Agreement to allocate responsibility for IMMEX Program compliance during the Transition Period, including responsibility for the filing of required IMMEX reports with Mexico\'s Ministry of Economy (*Secretaría de Economía*) and the maintenance of temporary importation records required under applicable Mexican customs regulations.

**Special Note Regarding Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility:** For the avoidance of doubt, the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility\'s environmental permits and compliance obligations are included in the Acquired Assets and shall be transferred to Buyer at Closing pursuant to Section 2.1. The Regulatory & EHS Compliance Transition Services with respect to the Pittsburgh Manufacturing Facility are limited to transitional compliance support to facilitate Buyer\'s assumption of direct responsibility for such permits and obligations, including assistance with permit transfer applications, compliance history documentation, and introduction to applicable regulatory agency contacts.
**[Category 6 --- Treasury & Tax]{.underline}**

**Description of Services:** Cash management services for the Business during the Transition Period, including cash concentration, disbursement, and intercompany settlement through Seller\'s existing treasury management infrastructure; bank account transition support, including assistance with the establishment of Buyer\'s own bank accounts and the orderly transfer of banking relationships; sales and use tax return preparation and filing for the Business; property tax return preparation and filing for the Facilities; and support for any ongoing tax audits or inquiries related to the pre-Closing operations of the Business, including document compilation, data retrieval, and coordination with Seller\'s tax department.
**Key Personnel / FTEs:** Approximately seven (7) full-time equivalent personnel, including treasury analysts, tax compliance specialists, and tax research analysts.
**Estimated Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost:** \$65,000
**Estimated Monthly TSA Fee (at 10% markup):** \$71,500
**Maximum Term:** Eighteen (18) months from the Closing Date.
**[Summary Fee Table]{.underline}**
**Service Category**               **Monthly Fully-Loaded Cost**   **Markup (%)**   **Monthly TSA Fee**   **FTEs**
Financial Reporting & Accounting   \$185,000                       10%              \$203,500             22
Information Technology             \$340,000                       10%              \$374,000             31
Supply Chain & Procurement         \$210,000                       10%              \$231,000             14
Regulatory & EHS Compliance        \$95,000                        10%              \$104,500             8

The estimated maximum aggregate TSA Fees for the full eighteen (18) month Maximum TSA Term, assuming all six categories of Transition Services are provided for the full Maximum TSA Term, are \$1,122,000 × 18 = **\$20,196,000**. Actual TSA Fees will vary based on actual Fully-Loaded Costs incurred and the duration of each category of Transition Services.
The foregoing estimates do not include any Additional Services that may be requested by Buyer and agreed to by Seller in accordance with Section 7.12(b) of the Agreement.
**[SIGNATURE PAGE]{.underline}**
**IN WITNESS WHEREOF**, the parties hereto have caused this Asset Purchase Agreement to be executed as of the date first written above by their respective officers thereunto duly authorized.

lines.text: **6. Key Terms --- Supply Agreements**

Service Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain Service Recipient\'s access to pricing under Service Provider\'s master supply agreements for the key raw material categories set forth above during the Term. Service Recipient acknowledges that pricing under such master supply agreements may be subject to volume-based adjustments and that Service Provider cannot guarantee that existing pricing will remain available if aggregate volumes (including Service Provider\'s own requirements) decline materially. Service Recipient shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate and establish its own supply agreements with key vendors prior to the expiration of the Term.
**7. Shared Warehouse --- Building 7**

The Parties acknowledge that Building 7 at Service Provider\'s Pittsburgh facility is a shared warehouse used by both the Business and Service Provider\'s Advanced Materials Division. During the Service Period, the Parties shall enter into a separate warehouse sharing arrangement for Building 7, detailing the allocation of warehouse space, access hours, security protocols, personnel responsibilities, and cost-sharing arrangements. Until such separate arrangement is finalized, the existing allocation of approximately 40% of Building 7 to the Business shall continue.
**8. Migration Milestones**

Service Recipient shall use commercially reasonable efforts to establish its own supply chain and procurement capabilities, including its own vendor relationships, logistics arrangements, and warehouse management systems, prior to the expiration of the Term. The Parties shall develop a vendor transition plan within ninety (90) days of the Effective Date.
**SCHEDULE E** **REGULATORY & EHS COMPLIANCE SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following regulatory and environmental, health, and safety (EHS) compliance services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **Environmental Permit Maintenance and Renewal.** Maintenance and renewal of environmental permits for the Greenville, South Carolina facility, including Clean Air Act Title V operating permits, Clean Water Act NPDES permits, and RCRA hazardous waste generator permits. Service Provider shall prepare and file renewal applications, respond to agency information requests, and coordinate permit modifications as necessary.

> \(b\) **OSHA Compliance Support.** Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) compliance support for the Pittsburgh and Greenville facilities, including safety audits and inspections, training program management (HAZCOM, lockout/tagout, confined space, fall protection), incident investigation and reporting (OSHA 300 logs), and safety program development and implementation.

> \(c\) **EPA Reporting.** Preparation and filing of reports required by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for the Greenville and Monterrey facilities, including Toxics Release Inventory (TRI) reports, RCRA Biennial Reports, Clean Air Act emissions inventories, and any other required environmental reports. For the Monterrey facility, Service Provider shall prepare corresponding reports required by Mexico\'s Secretaría de Medio Ambiente y Recursos Naturales (SEMARNAT) and relevant state environmental agencies.

> \(d\) **Environmental Monitoring and Testing.** Coordination of ongoing environmental monitoring and testing activities at the Greenville and Pittsburgh facilities, including air emissions monitoring, wastewater sampling and analysis, groundwater monitoring (as applicable), and stormwater management program compliance.

> \(e\) **Regulatory Filing Preparation.** Preparation of regulatory filings, registrations, and submissions required by Governmental Authorities in connection with the Business\'s manufacturing operations, including chemical substance registrations under TSCA (Toxic Substances Control Act) and any required updates to existing registrations.
**2. Service Provider Personnel**
Service Provider shall assign approximately eight (8) full-time equivalent personnel to provide the Regulatory & EHS Compliance Services, including the following roles:
**Role**                            **FTE Count**
EHS Director                        1
Environmental Compliance Manager    1
EHS Specialists                     3
Regulatory Affairs Analyst          1
Industrial Hygienist                1
Safety Trainer                      1
**3. Systems and Tools**

The following systems and tools shall be used in the delivery of the Regulatory & EHS Compliance Services: Service Provider\'s EHS management system, regulatory tracking database, OSHA recordkeeping system, and environmental monitoring data management platform.
**4. Service Period**
From the Effective Date through the earlier of: (a) termination of this Service in accordance with Article 5; or (b) expiration of the Term.
**5. Fees**
**Base Monthly Cost:**              **\$95,000**
Markup:                             10%
Monthly Fee:                        \$104,500
**6. Monterrey Facility --- Environmental and Safety Compliance**

Service Provider shall provide environmental and safety compliance support for the Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico facility, including coordination with SEMARNAT, PROFEPA (Procuraduría Federal de Protección al Ambiente), and applicable state environmental agencies with respect to environmental permits, emissions reporting, hazardous waste management, and workplace safety compliance under applicable Mexican NOM (Normas Oficiales Mexicanas) standards. Service Provider shall assist with the preparation of the Annual Operating Certificate (Cédula de Operación Anual --- COA) filing for the Monterrey facility.
**7. Migration Milestones**

Service Recipient shall use commercially reasonable efforts to develop and implement its own EHS management system and regulatory compliance capabilities prior to the expiration of the Term. Service Provider shall cooperate with the transition of environmental permits, registrations, and compliance records to Service Recipient. The Parties shall develop a regulatory transition plan within sixty (60) days of the Effective Date identifying all permits, registrations, and filings that must be transferred to or assumed by Service Recipient.
**8. Assumptions and Dependencies**

The Fees and scope of Services set forth in this Schedule E are based upon the following assumptions: (a) no material changes in environmental regulations affecting the Business\'s manufacturing operations during the Service Period; (b) Service Recipient provides timely access to manufacturing facilities for inspections, monitoring, and audits; and (c) Service Recipient promptly notifies Service Provider of any environmental incidents, spills, releases, or regulatory inquiries affecting the Business.
**SCHEDULE F** **TREASURY & TAX SERVICES**
**1. Service Description**
Service Provider shall provide the following treasury and tax services to Service Recipient during the applicable Service Period:

> \(a\) **Cash Management Support.** Assistance with bank account transition, including coordination with financial institutions to transfer or establish accounts in Service Recipient\'s name; wind-down of Service Provider\'s cash pooling arrangements to the extent they include the Business; and intercompany settlement of outstanding balances between Service Provider and the Business as of the Closing Date.

> \(b\) **Sales and Use Tax Filings.** Preparation and filing of sales and use Tax returns for the Business in all applicable jurisdictions in the United States, including calculation of Tax liability, reconciliation of Tax collected, and preparation of exemption certificate files.

> \(c\) **Property Tax Filings.** Preparation and filing of property Tax returns for real and personal property at the Pittsburgh, Greenville, and Monterrey manufacturing facilities, including valuation analysis, assessment review, and protest/appeal support.

> \(d\) **Tax Provision Support.** Assistance with the preparation of the income Tax provision for the Business for the stub period (from January 1, 2025 through the Closing Date) and for the post-Closing transition period, including current and deferred Tax calculations, effective Tax rate analysis, and preparation of Tax-related footnotes for the Business\'s financial statements.

> \(e\) **Transfer Pricing Documentation Support.** Assistance with the preparation and maintenance of transfer pricing documentation for intercompany transactions involving the Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico facility during the transition period, including preparation of the local transfer pricing study required under Mexico\'s Income Tax Law (Ley del Impuesto sobre la Renta) and support for any transfer pricing documentation required by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service under Section 482 and Treasury Regulations Section 1.6662-6.
**2. Service Provider Personnel**
Service Provider shall assign approximately seven (7) full-time equivalent personnel to provide the Treasury & Tax Services, including the following roles:
**Role**                            **FTE Count**
Tax Director                        1
Senior Tax Accountants              2
Treasury Analysts                   2
Tax Compliance Specialists          2
**3. Systems and Tools**

The following systems and tools shall be used in the delivery of the Treasury & Tax Services: SAP S/4HANA (Treasury module), Service Provider\'s Tax preparation software (Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE or equivalent), banking platforms, and transfer pricing analysis tools.
**4. Service Period**
From the Effective Date through the earlier of: (a) termination of this Service in accordance with Article 5; or (b) expiration of the Term.
**5. Fees**
**Base Monthly Cost:**              **\$65,000**
Markup:                             10%
Monthly Fee:                        \$71,500
**6. Migration Milestones**

> \(a\) **Bank Accounts.** Service Recipient shall establish its own bank accounts within thirty (30) days of the Closing Date. Service Provider shall cooperate with the orderly transition of banking relationships, including providing authorized signatories, account details, and historical banking records as reasonably requested.

> \(b\) **Intercompany Settlement.** All intercompany balances between Service Provider and the Business outstanding as of the Closing Date shall be settled within ninety (90) days of the Closing Date, in accordance with the settlement procedures set forth in the Purchase Agreement.

> \(c\) **Tax Filing Responsibilities.** Service Recipient shall assume responsibility for all Tax filings (sales and use, property, income, and other) for the Business by the twelfth (12th) month following the Closing Date. Service Provider shall cooperate with the transition of Tax filing responsibilities, including providing historical Tax returns, workpapers, and supporting documentation.
**7. Assumptions and Dependencies**

The Fees and scope of Services set forth in this Schedule F are based upon the following assumptions: (a) the number and complexity of Tax filings required for the Business will remain consistent with historical levels; (b) no material Tax audits, investigations, or disputes arise with respect to the Business during the Service Period that would require extraordinary effort by Service Provider; and (c) Service Recipient provides timely information and approvals necessary for the preparation of Tax returns and Tax provisions.
**SCHEDULE G** **FEE SCHEDULE**
**1. Monthly Service Fees**

The following table sets forth the monthly Fees for each Service category during the Term. All Fees are calculated on a cost-plus basis in accordance with Section 7.12(b) of the Purchase Agreement, reflecting Service Provider\'s fully-loaded cost of providing the applicable Service, plus the markup percentage indicated.

Financial Reporting & Accounting   A              \$185,000               10%              \$203,500
Information Technology             B              \$340,000               15%              \$391,000
Human Resources                    C              \$125,000               10%              \$137,500
Supply Chain & Procurement         D              \$210,000               10%              \$231,000

**2. Payment Terms**

Fees are payable monthly in arrears in accordance with Article 6 of this Agreement. Invoices shall be delivered by Service Provider within fifteen (15) Business Days after the end of each calendar month.
**3. Proration**

Fees for any partial calendar month (including the first and last months of the Service Period for any individual Service) shall be prorated on a daily basis, calculated as the applicable Monthly Fee divided by the number of calendar days in such month, multiplied by the number of calendar days during which such Service was provided.
**4. Additional Charges**

Unless expressly set forth in this Schedule G or the applicable Service Schedule, no additional charges shall be assessed by Service Provider for the provision of the Services. Any out-of-pocket costs or expenses incurred by Service Provider in connection with the Services (including travel, third-party vendor fees, and materials) are included in the Base Monthly Cost set forth above and shall not be separately invoiced to Service Recipient without Service Recipient\'s prior written approval.
**5. Fee Adjustment**

Fees are not subject to escalation or adjustment during the Term except as expressly provided in Article 6 of this Agreement. The Fees set forth in this Schedule G shall remain fixed for the duration of the Initial Term and any Renewal Terms.

from pathlib import Path
import re, os
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor

from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.enum.style import WD_STYLE_TYPE

ROOT = Path('.')
OUT = ROOT / 'output'
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
lines = (ROOT / 'draft.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines()

def clean(s):
    s = s.replace('\\\'', "'").replace('\\"','"').replace('\\[','[').replace('\\] ','] ')
    s = re.sub(r'\{\.underline\}', '', s)
    s = s.replace('**','').replace('*','')
    s = s.replace('\\(', '(').replace('\\)', ')')
    s = s.replace('\\$', '$').replace('\\%', '%')
    s = s.replace('\\_', '_')
    s = s.replace('\\-', '-')
    s = s.replace('\\', '')
    s = re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?', '', s)
    return s.strip()

def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge); element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); tcBorders.append(element)
            for k,v in kwargs[edge].items(): element.set(qn('w:'+k), str(v))

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top',top),('start',start),('bottom',bottom),('end',end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None: node = OxmlElement('w:'+m); tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def add_page_number(paragraph):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = 'PAGE'
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)

def setup(doc, title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(.7); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(.7); sec.left_margin = Inches(.75); sec.right_margin = Inches(.75)

    if 'Clause' not in styles:
        st=styles.add_style('Clause', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH); st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(9); st.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(4)
    header = sec.header.paragraphs[0]
    header.text = 'PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT WORK PRODUCT'
    header.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    header.runs[0].font.name='Arial'; header.runs[0].font.size=Pt(8); header.runs[0].font.bold=True; header.runs[0].font.color.rgb=RGBColor(100,100,100)
    footer = sec.footer.paragraphs[0]; footer.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER

def clean(s):
    s = s.replace('\\\'', "'").replace('\\"','"').replace('\\[','[').replace('\\] ','] ')
    s = re.sub(r'\{\.underline\}', '', s)
    s = s.replace('**','').replace('*','')
    s = s.replace('\\(', '(').replace('\\)', ')')
    s = s.replace('\\$', '$').replace('\\%', '%')
    s = s.replace('\\_', '_')
    s = s.replace('\\-', '-')
    s = s.replace('\\', '')
    s = re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?', '', s)
    return s.strip()

def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge); element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); tcBorders.append(element)
            for k,v in kwargs[edge].items(): element.set(qn('w:'+k), str(v))

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top',top),('start',start),('bottom',bottom),('end',end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None: node = OxmlElement('w:'+m); tcMar.append(node)
        node.set(qn('w:w'), str(v)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')

def set_repeat_table_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); tblHeader = OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)

def add_page_number(paragraph):
    run = paragraph.add_run()
    fldChar1 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar1.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'begin')
    instrText = OxmlElement('w:instrText'); instrText.set(qn('xml:space'), 'preserve'); instrText.text = 'PAGE'
    fldChar2 = OxmlElement('w:fldChar'); fldChar2.set(qn('w:fldCharType'), 'end')
    run._r.append(fldChar1); run._r.append(instrText); run._r.append(fldChar2)

def setup(doc, title):
    sec = doc.sections[0]
    sec.top_margin = Inches(.7); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(.7); sec.left_margin = Inches(.75); sec.right_margin = Inches(.75)
    styles = doc.styles
    styles['Normal'].font.name='Arial'; styles['Normal'].font.size=Pt(9)
    for name, size, color in [('Heading 1',15,'17365D'),('Heading 2',12,'1F4E79'),('Heading 3',10,'1F4E79')]:
        st=styles[name]; st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(size); st.font.bold=True; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor.from_string(color)
    if 'Small Note' not in styles:
        st=styles.add_style('Small Note', WD_STYLE_TYPE.PARAGRAPH); st.font.name='Arial'; st.font.size=Pt(8); st.font.italic=True; st.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(90,90,90)

def add_source_line(doc, s):
    c=clean(s)
    if not c: return
    if c.startswith('---') or c.startswith('___'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=p.add_run(c); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(100,100,100); return
    if c.startswith('ARTICLE ') or c.startswith('SCHEDULE ') or c.startswith('[ARTICLE') or c.startswith('[SCHEDULE') or c.startswith('[SIGNATURE') or c.startswith('[TRANSITION'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2'); p.add_run(c); return
    if re.match(r'^Section\s+\d', c):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 3'); m=re.match(r'^(Section\s+[\d.]+)(.*)$',c)
        p.add_run(m.group(1)).bold=True; p.add_run(m.group(2)); return
    if c.startswith('DRAFT ---') or c.startswith('TABLE OF CONTENTS'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; p.add_run(c).bold=True; return
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Clause');
    if c.startswith(('>','(a)','(b)','(c)','(d)','(e)','(f)')): p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(.2)
    r=p.add_run(c); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)

def original_text(start, end=None):
    if end is None: end=start
    return '\n'.join(clean(lines[i-1]) for i in range(start,end+1) if clean(lines[i-1]))

def add_redline_box(doc, cid, tier, title, deleted, added, basis, risk, position):
    table=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2); table.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    table.autofit=False; table.columns[0].width=Inches(4.65); table.columns[1].width=Inches(2.15)
    left,right=table.rows[0].cells; left.width=Inches(4.65); right.width=Inches(2.15)
    for c in (left,right): set_cell_margins(c, top=100, start=120, bottom=100, end=120); set_cell_border(c, top={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, left={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, right={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'})
    set_cell_shading(right, 'FFF2CC' if tier=='Critical' else 'EAF3F8')
    p=left.paragraphs[0]; p.style='Heading 3'; p.add_run(title)
    p=left.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(3); r=p.add_run('DELETE — '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(192,0,0); r2=p.add_run(deleted); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(192,0,0); r2.font.strike=True
    p=left.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=p.add_run('ADD — '); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0,102,204); r2=p.add_run(added); r2.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(0,102,204); r2.font.underline=True
    p=right.paragraphs[0]; r=p.add_run(f'COMMENT {cid}'); r.bold=True; r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(31,78,121)
    p=right.add_paragraph(); r=p.add_run(f'{tier} — {position}'); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(8)
    for label,text in [('Basis',basis),('Risk',risk),('Position',position)]:
        p=right.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=p.add_run(label+': '); r.bold=True; r.font.size=Pt(7.5); r2=p.add_run(text); r2.font.size=Pt(7.5)
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(1)

def add_insert_box(doc, cid, tier, title, added, basis, risk, position):
    add_redline_box(doc,cid,tier,title,'[No provision in draft]',added,basis,risk,position)

def block_end(start):
    # start is one-based; find next major section/article/schedule heading
    for j in range(start, len(lines)+1):
        if j==start: continue
        s=lines[j-1].strip()
        if (s.startswith('**Section ') or s.startswith('**[ARTICLE') or s.startswith('**[SCHEDULE') or s.startswith('**SCHEDULE ') or s.startswith('**[SIGNATURE') or s.startswith('**[TRANSITION')):
            return j-1
    return len(lines)

    s = s.replace('\\\'', "'").replace('\\"','"').replace('\\[','[').replace('\\] ','] ')
    s = re.sub(r'\{\.underline\}', '', s)
    s = s.replace('**','').replace('*','')
    s = s.replace('\\(', '(').replace('\\)', ')')
    s = s.replace('\\$', '$').replace('\\%', '%')
    s = s.replace('\\_', '_')
    s = s.replace('\\-', '-')
    s = s.replace('\\', '')
    s = re.sub(r'^\s*>\s?', '', s)
    return s.strip()

def set_cell_shading(cell, fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = tcPr.find(qn('w:shd'))
    if shd is None:
        shd = OxmlElement('w:shd'); tcPr.append(shd)
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'), fill)

def set_cell_border(cell, **kwargs):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcBorders = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcBorders')
    if tcBorders is None:
        tcBorders = OxmlElement('w:tcBorders'); tcPr.append(tcBorders)
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        if edge in kwargs:
            tag = 'w:{}'.format(edge); element = tcBorders.find(qn(tag))
            if element is None:
                element = OxmlElement(tag); tcBorders.append(element)
            for k,v in kwargs[edge].items(): element.set(qn('w:'+k), str(v))

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=80, start=100, bottom=80, end=100):
    tc = cell._tc; tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr(); tcMar = tcPr.first_child_found_in('w:tcMar')
    if tcMar is None:
        tcMar = OxmlElement('w:tcMar'); tcPr.append(tcMar)
    for m, v in [('top',top),('start',start),('bottom',bottom),('end',end)]:
        node = tcMar.find(qn('w:'+m))
        if node is None: node = OxmlElement('w:'+m); tcMar.append(node)

def set_repeat_table_header(row):

def add_source_line(doc, s):
    c=clean(s)
    if not c: return
    if c.startswith('---') or c.startswith('___'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2); r=p.add_run(c); r.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(100,100,100); return
    if c.startswith('ARTICLE ') or c.startswith('SCHEDULE ') or c.startswith('[ARTICLE') or c.startswith('[SCHEDULE') or c.startswith('[SIGNATURE') or c.startswith('[TRANSITION'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 2'); p.add_run(c); return
    if re.match(r'^Section\s+\d', c):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Heading 3'); m=re.match(r'^(Section\s+[\d.]+)(.*)$',c)
        p.add_run(m.group(1)).bold=True; p.add_run(m.group(2)); return
    if c.startswith('DRAFT ---') or c.startswith('TABLE OF CONTENTS'):
        p=doc.add_paragraph(); p.alignment=WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER; p.add_run(c).bold=True; return
    p=doc.add_paragraph(style='Clause');
    if c.startswith(('>','(a)','(b)','(c)','(d)','(e)','(f)')): p.paragraph_format.left_indent=Inches(.2)
    r=p.add_run(c); r.font.name='Arial'; r.font.size=Pt(8.5)

def original_text(start, end=None):
    if end is None: end=start
    return '\n'.join(clean(lines[i-1]) for i in range(start,end+1) if clean(lines[i-1]))

    for c in (left,right): set_cell_margins(c, top=100, start=120, bottom=100, end=120); set_cell_border(c, top={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, bottom={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, left={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'}, right={'val':'single','sz':'6','color':'B7C9D6'})
    set_cell_shading(right, 'FFF2CC' if tier=='Critical' else 'EAF3F8')

def block_end(start):
    # start is one-based; find next major section/article/schedule heading
    for j in range(start, len(lines)+1):
        if j==start: continue
        s=lines[j-1].strip()
        if (s.startswith('**Section ') or s.startswith('**[ARTICLE') or s.startswith('**[SCHEDULE') or s.startswith('**SCHEDULE ') or s.startswith('**[SIGNATURE') or s.startswith('**[TRANSITION')):
            return j-1
    return len(lines)

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL**

**TSA REVIEW MEMORANDUM --- SELLER-SIDE PRIORITY ANALYSIS**

*Prepared for Polaris Industrial Holdings, Inc. \| Seller-side review \| May 2025*

**PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- SUBJECT TO ATTORNEY-CLIENT PRIVILEGE AND WORK-PRODUCT PROTECTION**

**To:** Victoria S. Andersen

**From:** Seller-side review team

**Re:** Polaris / Trident --- Specialty Coatings Divestiture TSA

**Date:** May 2025

# Executive summary

The Trident draft is not ready for circulation or signature. It contains multiple direct conflicts with APA §7.12 and Exhibit H, including the service standard, automatic renewal, 120-day service termination notice, the liability cap, the one-way consequential-damages waiver, the IP license, the IT fee markup, and omitted Monterrey IMMEX / Mexican data-processing mechanics. These are must-change items. The draft also departs materially from the Polaris playbook on staffing discretion, termination assistance, payment and escalation mechanics, indemnification, data ownership, insurance, audit rights, force-majeure termination, governing law / dispute resolution, change orders, and non-solicitation.

The proposed redline corrects those points while preserving a practical transition structure: Trident is required to build independent capability quickly; Polaris retains workforce and systems flexibility; the parties have defined wind-down and migration mechanics; and the Monterrey risks are allocated to the post-Closing operator with substantive privacy safeguards.

# Priority 1 --- Critical: direct APA conflicts / must-change

**C1 --- Service standard (§3.1)**

Replace the 24-month "at least equal to or better than" and industry-best-practices standard with the APA's 12-month "substantially consistent" benchmark. Add that Polaris need not prioritize Trident or adopt new methodologies or best practices. Basis: APA §§7.12(a), 7.12(f). Risk: an external or ratcheting standard could make ordinary historical variation a breach and force Polaris to devote resources ahead of retained businesses. Position: firm.

**C2 --- Term / automatic renewal (§5.2)**

Delete automatic renewal. The base term is 18 months; any extension must be a mutually signed written amendment and may not exceed six months for an affected Service. Basis: APA §7.12(a). Risk: automatic renewal could create an unapproved service obligation and undermine migration incentives. Position: firm.

**C3 --- Termination notice (§5.3)**

Change 120 days to 90 days and preserve Buyer's responsibility for accrued Fees and non-cancelable commitments. Basis: APA §7.12(c) establishes the minimum and maximum period. Risk: a 120-day lock-in is a direct conflict and restricts Polaris's ability to exit inefficient services. Position: firm.

**C4 --- Fees / IT markup (§6.1; Schedule B; Schedule G)**

Correct Information Technology from 15% / \$391,000 per month to 10% / \$374,000 per month. Require a category-by-category 10% ceiling. Draft monthly total is \$1,139,000; Exhibit H is \$1,122,000. Over 18 months, the draft total is \$20,502,000 versus \$20,196,000 under Exhibit H --- a \$306,000 difference. Basis: APA §7.12(b) and Exhibit H. Even though the error favors Polaris, correct it for APA compliance and credibility. Position: firm.

**C5 --- Liability cap (§10.1)**

Replace 200% of cumulative fees with the APA trailing-12-month cap, including the first-12-month actual-paid convention and the APA carve-outs. Assuming all categories run at \$1.122 million/month, the draft could produce a \$40.392 million cap at month 18 (200% × \$20.196 million) versus \$13.464 million under the APA --- a \$26.928 million delta. At month 12, the draft would be \$26.928 million versus \$13.464 million under the APA. Basis: APA §7.12(d). Position: firm.

**C6 --- Consequential damages (§10.2)**

Make the waiver mutual, with the APA third-party indemnity carve-out. The current clause waives only Polaris's claims and leaves Trident free to pursue business interruption, lost profits, replacement costs, or similar consequential damages. Basis: APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.2. Position: firm.

**C7 --- IP license (§7.1)**

Delete the perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license to Polaris tools, methodologies, processes, software, and know-how. Reserve ownership and allow only the access necessary to receive Services during the Service Period. Basis: APA §7.12(e)(ii); Playbook §6.1; client instructions. Position: firm / board-level IP concern.

**C8 --- Monterrey cross-border gaps (new §§2.6, 8.4--8.5)**

Add operative IMMEX allocation and LFPDPPP processing terms. Trident has primary responsibility and cost for post-Closing IMMEX compliance, records, notices, and filings; Polaris provides specified transition assistance only. For Mexican employee data, Trident is controller and must provide notices/consents or another lawful mechanism; Polaris is processor on documented instructions with safeguards and breach notification. Basis: APA §7.12(g); Exhibit H; Playbook §§6.3 and 12; client instructions. Risk: duty/tax consequences from an IMMEX lapse and privacy enforcement exposure for 300+ Mexican employees. Position: firm, subject to Mexico counsel confirmation of local-law mechanics.

# Priority 2 --- Significant: major playbook deviations

**C9 --- Staffing / key personnel (§4.3; Schedule H)**

Delete Trident's prior written consent right and any minimum FTE allocation. Retain Polaris sole discretion; offer 15 Business Days' advance notice for reassignment/replacement on the agreed list and reasonable replacement efforts. This is a reasonable compromise, but consent is unacceptable. Basis: Playbook §7.1.

**C10 --- Termination assistance (§5.5; new text)**

Add a defined wind-down: up to 60 days, cost-plus-15%, covering knowledge transfer, data migration support, replacement-provider cooperation, and documentation. No assistance while undisputed invoices remain unpaid. Basis: Playbook §3.4. This avoids an implied indefinite post-termination duty.

**C11 --- Payment and escalation (§§6.3--6.4; Schedule G)**

Replace "commercially reasonable time" with Net 30, late interest at the lesser of 1.5% per month or the legal maximum, and payment of undisputed portions. Add annual escalation by the greater of 3% or CPI-U, plus an escalation event mechanism for law, vendor, or material volume changes. CPI-U only is a fallback. Basis: Playbook §§4.2--4.3.

**C12 --- Indemnification (§§9.1--9.2)**

Limit indemnification to third-party claims; keep Trident's use/reliance indemnity broad but fault-based; limit Polaris indemnity to third-party claims caused by gross negligence or willful misconduct; subject indemnities to the cap and consequential-damages waiver. Basis: Playbook §5.3 and APA §7.12(d).

**C13 --- Data / systems ownership (§7.2)**

Reserve Polaris pre-Closing data, system-level data, databases, configurations, security tools, and systems. Define post-Closing Business data generated for Trident as Buyer Data and provide reasonable paid extraction assistance. Basis: Playbook §6.2.

**C14 --- Buyer insurance (§13.1)**

Raise CGL to \$5 million per occurrence / aggregate and add \$5 million umbrella or excess, statutory workers' compensation, additional-insured status for Polaris, waiver of subrogation, and certificate/endorsement delivery within 10 Business Days and annually. Playbook fallback is \$3 million CGL / umbrella if needed.

**C15 --- Audit rights (§§14.1--14.2)**

Move to once per 12 months, 30 Business Days' notice, Trident expense, fee-related records only, no proprietary systems or internal cost methodologies, confidentiality, and a 5% overcharge threshold before Polaris reimburses reasonable audit costs. A 20-day notice fallback is acceptable. Basis: Playbook §9.1.

**C16 --- Force majeure (§12.1)**

Add a 90-consecutive-day termination right for an affected Service, with 120 days as the maximum fallback. Basis: Playbook §10.1.

**C17 --- Governing law / dispute resolution (§§15.1--15.2)**

Replace Ohio law and Cuyahoga County litigation with Pennsylvania law and executive escalation followed by optional mediation and confidential AAA arbitration in Pittsburgh before one experienced arbitrator. New York or Philadelphia is a location fallback; litigation is not. Basis: Playbook §11.

**C18 --- Non-solicitation (new §15.12)**

Add a 12-month post-termination restriction on soliciting/hiring Service Provider personnel, with general-solicitation and no-cause-termination exceptions. Six months is the absolute fallback. Basis: Playbook §7.2.

**C19 --- Change orders (new §2.5)**

Require a signed change order for out-of-scope services, material volume increases, or scope changes; price at cost-plus-15% (10% absolute fallback); no obligation before signature and any advance payment; acceptance in Polaris's sole discretion. Basis: Playbook §4.4.

# Priority 3 --- Minor: negotiation preferences and cleanup

**C20 --- Service-provider representations (§11.2)**

Narrow the capacity and legal-compliance representations to the resources then deployed, the agreed scope, Applicable Law, third-party restrictions, and the historical service standard. If Trident insists, this is negotiable but should not become an independent warranty of uninterrupted performance.

**Schedule consistency**

Conform Schedule B's fee line and Schedule G's total; confirm all six categories use the Exhibit H estimates and 10% markup. Remove any inconsistency between Schedule H and §4.3 regarding consent, FTE minimums, and replacements.

**Operational drafting**

Retain the existing monthly invoice cadence (within 15 Business Days) and three-year confidentiality survival. The existing APA precedence clause in §15.5 is helpful and should remain. Confirm the final TSA date, Effective Date, notice addresses, and cross-references before execution.

# Quantified exposure and fee check

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Item                        Draft                            APA / proposed                      Delta
  --------------------------- -------------------------------- ----------------------------------- ------------------
  Monthly IT fee              \$391,000 (15%)                  \$374,000 (10%)                     \$17,000 / month

  Monthly aggregate fee       \$1,139,000                      \$1,122,000                         \$17,000 / month

  18-month aggregate fee      \$20,502,000                     \$20,196,000                        \$306,000

  Liability cap at month 18   \$40,392,000 (200% cumulative)   \$13,464,000 (trailing 12 months)   \$26,928,000
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assumptions: all six service categories continue for the full 18 months; all invoices are paid; fees remain at the Exhibit H estimates. Actual cap amounts will vary with actual Fees and claim timing. The APA cap is measured when the claim is first asserted in writing and uses actual paid Fees during the first 12 months, then a rolling 12-month lookback.

# Recommended negotiation posture

- Lead with the eight Critical items as APA conformity and closing-readiness points. Do not trade away the trailing-12-month cap, mutual damages waiver, no-license position, 90-day notice, or 18-month/no-automatic-renewal structure.

- Use the cross-border language as the substantive opening position. Ask Mexico counsel to confirm the final LFPDPPP notice/consent and IMMEX mechanics, but do not leave the TSA silent or use a placeholder.

- Offer reasonable flexibility on staffing notice, CPI-U-only escalation, 20-day audit notice, 120-day force-majeure termination, and a shorter non-solicitation period only if necessary. Require General Counsel escalation before conceding below the playbook fallbacks.

- Correct the fee error even though it currently benefits Polaris. It is an APA compliance issue and correcting it supports credibility with Trident and avoids later reconciliation disputes.

# Closing recommendation

Transmit the redline only after internal approval by Victoria and Sharon. The most alarming items for the May 1 status discussion are the \$26.928 million potential liability-cap delta, the perpetual enterprise-wide IP license, the unilateral consequential-damages waiver, the 15% IT markup, and the absence of IMMEX / LFPDPPP terms. These should be described as must-change items affecting risk allocation and closing readiness, not ordinary drafting preferences.

No license, sublicense, right to use, right to copy, right to modify, or other interest is granted to Service Recipient, except the limited access necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period. All access ends when the applicable Service ends.','APA §7.12(e)(ii); Playbook §6.1.','The perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license could expose Polaris’s enterprise-wide operational IP and allow modification, derivative works, and sublicensing.','Firm — no TSA license; any post-transition license must be separately negotiated.'),

385: ('C13','Significant','Section 7.2 — Data and Systems', original_text(385), 'Service Recipient owns data relating exclusively to the Business that is generated after Closing (“Buyer Data”). Service Provider retains ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, databases, configurations, security tools, and other Service Provider Data. Polaris shall provide reasonable data extraction and transfer assistance at the end of a Service, subject to payment of applicable Fees and reasonable security controls; no transfer grants access to Polaris systems or IP.','Playbook §6.2.','Without a reservation, Trident could characterize Polaris’s shared systems, pre-Closing data, and system-derived information as Buyer materials and demand broad return or destruction.','Firm — preserve Polaris ownership while supporting orderly migration.'),

407: ('C8','Critical','Section 8.4 — Data Privacy', original_text(407), 'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data-protection laws, including U.S. laws and Mexico’s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. For Mexican employee data, Trident is the data controller and Polaris is the processor/service provider acting only on Trident’s documented instructions. Trident shall provide or cause to be provided compliant avisos de privacidad and obtain any required consents or other lawful transfer mechanisms before data is transferred to or processed by Polaris. Polaris shall maintain appropriate technical and organizational safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, assist with legally required notices and data-subject requests to the extent reasonably requested, and notify Trident without undue delay (and in any event within 48 hours after confirmation) of a data-security incident affecting Mexican employee data.','APA §7.12(g)(ii); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','The U.S.-only clause omits the LFPDPPP, privacy notices, lawful transfer mechanism, processor/controller allocation, and incident mechanics for 300+ Mexican employees.','Firm — use this as operative interim language pending Mexico counsel confirmation.'),

411: ('C12','Significant','Section 9.1 — Service Recipient Indemnification', original_text(411,419), 'Service Recipient shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Service Provider Indemnitees from third-party claims arising out of Service Recipient’s use of or reliance on the Services or deliverables, breach of this Agreement, or negligent or wrongful acts or omissions of Service Recipient or its personnel, except to the extent caused by Service Provider’s gross negligence or willful misconduct. The indemnity is subject to the aggregate liability cap and the consequential-damages waiver.','Playbook §5.3.','The draft’s “any and all Losses” formulation is not limited to third-party claims and could create uncapped direct indemnity exposure for ordinary contractual disputes.','Firm — limit to third-party claims and preserve the cap.'),

421: ('C12','Significant','Section 9.2 — Service Provider Indemnification', original_text(421,427), 'Service Provider shall indemnify Service Recipient only for third-party claims to the extent arising from Service Provider’s gross negligence or willful misconduct in performing the Services. This indemnity is subject to the aggregate liability cap and the consequential-damages waiver.','Playbook §5.3; APA §7.12(d).','The draft creates direct indemnity for any breach and any legal violation, bypassing the negotiated liability allocation and potentially swallowing the cap carve-outs.','Firm — retain the gross-negligence / willful-misconduct threshold.'),

441: ('C5','Critical','Section 10.1 — Aggregate Liability Cap', original_text(441), 'Service Provider’s aggregate liability under or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the total TSA Fees actually paid by Service Recipient during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the date the applicable claim is first asserted in writing. During the first twelve (12) months after Closing, the cap equals Fees actually paid from Closing through assertion; thereafter it is measured on a rolling twelve-month basis. The cap excludes only the APA-mandated categories: fraud or willful misconduct, confidentiality breaches, and third-party indemnification claims to the extent caused by the indemnifying party’s gross negligence, fraud, or willful misconduct.','APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.1.','Assuming all categories run at $1.122 million/month, the draft could reach $40.392 million at month 18 (200% × $20.196 million), versus the APA cap of $13.464 million (trailing 12 months). Delta: $26.928 million.','Firm — the APA-mandated cap is not negotiable.'),

443: ('C6','Critical','Section 10.2 — Consequential Damages', original_text(443), 'NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, INCLUDING LOST PROFITS, LOST REVENUE, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITY, COST OF REPLACEMENT SERVICES, DIMINUTION OF VALUE, OR LOSS OF GOODWILL, ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THIS AGREEMENT, REGARDLESS OF THEORY OR NOTICE OF POSSIBILITY; PROVIDED THAT THIS SENTENCE SHALL NOT LIMIT LIABILITY FOR THIRD-PARTY CLAIMS SUBJECT TO INDEMNIFICATION UNDER THIS AGREEMENT.','APA §7.12(d); Playbook §5.2.','The draft waives only Polaris’s claims and leaves Polaris exposed to Trident’s potentially very large consequential-damages claims.','Firm — mutuality is mandatory.'),

461: ('C20','Minor','Section 11.2 — Service Provider Representations', original_text(461,467), 'Service Provider represents only that, as of the Effective Date, it intends to provide the Services in accordance with this Agreement using the resources then deployed to the Business, subject to the scope limitations, historical service standard, Applicable Law, and third-party contractual restrictions. No representation is made that Polaris will maintain any particular employee, system, or capability beyond those obligations.','Playbook §§2.1–2.2; risk allocation.','The current representation is broader than the operative service covenant and could be used to create an independent warranty of capacity, legal compliance, and uninterrupted performance.','Negotiable — narrow if Trident insists on a representation.'),

473: ('C16','Significant','Section 12.1 — Force Majeure', original_text(473), 'Neither Party shall be liable for delay or nonperformance caused by a Force Majeure Event after prompt notice and commercially reasonable mitigation efforts. If a Force Majeure Event materially affects an individual Service for ninety (90) consecutive days, either Party may terminate that affected Service on written notice without further liability, except for accrued Fees, non-cancelable commitments, and obligations that survive.','Playbook §10.1.','Without a termination trigger, Polaris may remain tied to an unavailable or uneconomic service indefinitely.','Firm — 90-day trigger; 120 days is the maximum fallback.'),

479: ('C14','Significant','Section 13.1 — Service Recipient Insurance', original_text(479), 'Service Recipient shall maintain during the Term and for twelve (12) months thereafter: (a) CGL insurance of at least $5,000,000 per occurrence and $5,000,000 aggregate; (b) $5,000,000 umbrella/excess liability; and (c) workers’ compensation at statutory limits. Polaris shall be named as an additional insured under the CGL and umbrella/excess policies, and the policies shall include a waiver of subrogation in Polaris’s favor. Certificates and endorsements shall be delivered within ten (10) Business Days after Closing and annually thereafter.','Playbook §8.1.','The draft provides only $2 million CGL, no umbrella, no additional-insured endorsement, no waiver of subrogation, and no certificate deadline.','Firm — accept no less than the $3 million fallback if necessary.'),

493: ('C15','Significant','Section 14.1 — Audit Rights', original_text(493), 'Service Recipient may audit Service Provider’s fee-related books and records no more than once in any twelve (12)-month period, at Service Recipient’s sole expense, on at least thirty (30) Business Days’ prior written notice. Audits shall occur during normal business hours, be limited to records reasonably necessary to verify Fees, exclude proprietary systems, internal cost methodologies, unrelated personnel records, and security-sensitive information, and be subject to confidentiality obligations. If an audit identifies an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) for the audited period, Service Provider shall credit the overcharge and reasonable audit costs.','Playbook §9.1.','Two audits per calendar year, ten days’ notice, Polaris-paid costs, and access to systems and personnel invite disruption and disclosure of proprietary information.','Firm — buyer bears its audit cost; a 20-business-day notice fallback is acceptable.'),

495: ('C15','Significant','Section 14.2 — Audit Adjustments', original_text(495), 'If an audit identifies an overcharge exceeding five percent (5%) for the audited period, Service Provider shall credit the overcharge within thirty (30) days after written demand and reimburse reasonable audit costs. If an audit identifies an undercharge, Service Recipient shall pay the deficiency within thirty (30) days. Any credit or payment shall be subject to the Agreement’s dispute procedures.','Playbook §9.1.','The draft requires Polaris to pay interest on every overcharge regardless of materiality and gives no threshold or reciprocal audit-cost rule.','Firm — retain a materiality threshold and buyer-funded audit default.'),

499: ('C17','Significant','Section 15.1 — Governing Law', original_text(499), 'This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles.','Playbook §11.1.','Ohio law gives Trident a home-state advantage and is inconsistent with Polaris’s standard position and Pittsburgh-centered administration.','Firm — Delaware is the only reasonable fallback if required by the APA.'),

501: ('C17','Significant','Section 15.2 — Dispute Resolution', original_text(501), 'Any dispute not resolved by senior-executive escalation within fifteen (15) Business Days may, at either Party’s option, be submitted to non-binding mediation and then resolved by confidential binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, before one arbitrator with relevant industry experience. The arbitrator may award only relief available under this Agreement.','Playbook §11.2.','Cuyahoga County court litigation creates public, buyer-home-jurisdiction proceedings and broader discovery risk.','Firm — do not accept litigation; New York or Philadelphia is a neutral fallback.'),

schedule_g=('C4','Critical','Schedule G — Fee Schedule', original_text(995,1034), 'The fee table shall reflect the Exhibit H amounts: Financial Reporting & Accounting $203,500; Information Technology $374,000; Human Resources $137,500; Supply Chain & Procurement $231,000; Regulatory & EHS Compliance $104,500; Treasury & Tax $71,500; total monthly Fees $1,122,000. The Fee Schedule shall also state that no category markup exceeds 10%, that actual Fully-Loaded Costs may be adjusted only as permitted by APA §7.12(b), and that Fees escalate only as provided in amended Section 6.4.','APA §7.12(b); Exhibit H; Playbook §§4.1–4.2.','The draft total is $1.139 million/month and $20.502 million over 18 months, versus $1.122 million/month and $20.196 million under Exhibit H.','Firm — correct the schedule even though the error favors Polaris; credibility and APA compliance control.')
