351: ('C3','Critical','Section 5.3 — Termination of Individual Services', original_text(351), 'Either Party may terminate any individual Service upon not less than ninety (90) days’ prior written notice to the other Party. Notice shall identify the Service and effective date. Buyer remains responsible for accrued Fees and non-cancelable commitments incurred before notice in reasonable reliance on continuation, subject to Polaris’s commercially reasonable mitigation efforts.','APA §7.12(c).','The draft’s 120-day period is outside the APA’s express minimum/maximum 90-day period and could lock Polaris into uneconomic service delivery.','Firm — APA conformity is not negotiable.'),
355: ('C10','Significant','Section 5.5 — Effect of Termination / Termination Assistance', original_text(355,363), 'Upon expiration or termination of any Service, Service Provider’s obligation to provide the affected Service ceases on the effective date, subject to accrued Fees and non-cancelable commitments. At Service Recipient’s written request delivered before termination, Service Provider shall provide reasonable termination assistance for up to sixty (60) days at cost-plus-fifteen percent (15%), including knowledge transfer, data migration support, cooperation with replacement providers, and transition documentation. Polaris has no termination-assistance obligation while undisputed amounts remain unpaid.','Playbook §3.4.','The draft ends Services immediately but is silent on a defined wind-down, leaving ambiguity and potential claims for indefinite cooperation.','Firm — define a short, compensated wind-down.'),
369: ('C4','Critical','Section 6.1 — Service Charges / 10% Cap', original_text(369), 'Fees shall be calculated for each Service category as Fully-Loaded Cost plus a markup not exceeding ten percent (10%) of the applicable Fully-Loaded Cost. The ten-percent cap applies to each category individually. Actual costs and adjustments shall be handled consistently with APA §7.12(b) and the applicable Fee Schedule.','APA §7.12(b); Exhibit H; Playbook §4.1.','The clause does not itself enforce the category-by-category cap, and Schedule B applies a 15% markup. The IT overcharge is $17,000 per month and $306,000 over 18 months if unchanged.','Firm — correct the IT markup and aggregate Fee Schedule.'),
383: ('C7','Critical','Section 7.1 — Service Provider Materials', original_text(383), 'All Service Provider Materials, including tools, methodologies, templates, processes, software, systems, and know-how, remain the sole and exclusive property of Service Provider. No license, sublicense, right to use, right to copy, right to modify, or other interest is granted to Service Recipient, except the limited access necessary to receive the Services during the applicable Service Period. All access ends when the applicable Service ends.','APA §7.12(e)(ii); Playbook §6.1.','The perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license could expose Polaris’s enterprise-wide operational IP and allow modification, derivative works, and sublicensing.','Firm — no TSA license; any post-transition license must be separately negotiated.'),
385: ('C13','Significant','Section 7.2 — Data and Systems', original_text(385), 'Service Recipient owns data relating exclusively to the Business that is generated after Closing (“Buyer Data”). Service Provider retains ownership of all pre-Closing data, system-level data, databases, configurations, security tools, and other Service Provider Data. Polaris shall provide reasonable data extraction and transfer assistance at the end of a Service, subject to payment of applicable Fees and reasonable security controls; no transfer grants access to Polaris systems or IP.','Playbook §6.2.','Without a reservation, Trident could characterize Polaris’s shared systems, pre-Closing data, and system-derived information as Buyer materials and demand broad return or destruction.','Firm — preserve Polaris ownership while supporting orderly migration.'),
407: ('C8','Critical','Section 8.4 — Data Privacy', original_text(407), 'Each Party shall comply with all applicable data-protection laws, including U.S. laws and Mexico’s Federal Law on Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (LFPDPPP) and its Regulations. For Mexican employee data, Trident is the data controller and Polaris is the processor/service provider acting only on Trident’s documented instructions. Trident shall provide or cause to be provided compliant avisos de privacidad and obtain any required consents or other lawful transfer mechanisms before data is transferred to or processed by Polaris. Polaris shall maintain appropriate technical and organizational safeguards, restrict access to personnel with a need to know, assist with legally required notices and data-subject requests to the extent reasonably requested, and notify Trident without undue delay (and in any event within 48 hours after confirmation) of a data-security incident affecting Mexican employee data.','APA §7.12(g)(ii); Playbook §6.3; client instructions.','The U.S.-only clause omits the LFPDPPP, privacy notices, lawful transfer mechanism, processor/controller allocation, and incident mechanics for 300+ Mexican employees.','Firm — use this as operative interim language pending Mexico counsel confirmation.'),
